application.quote: A Financial Assistance application will need to be re-submitted if more than six months has transpired since initial denial.

notes: The policy states that financial assistance determinations are made after all efforts to qualify the patient for other public or private programs have been exhausted, but does not specify a exact timeframe for when the patient must apply beyond the 6-month reapplication rule after denial.

The policy mentions that financial assistance will be applied to all eligible accounts incurred for services received prior to application date if eligibility is approved, for a period of twelve months.
The policy does not specify a maximum percentage of monthly income for payment plans or a minimum monthly payment amount.
The policy does not state when extraordinary collection actions (ECA) may begin, only that reasonable efforts to determine eligibility must be made first.
The policy defines 'Medically Necessary' as services or items reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis or treatment of illness or injury, as defined by Medicare.

The policy defines 'Underinsured Patient' as an individual with private or public insurance coverage for whom it would be a financial hardship to fully pay the expected out-of-pocket expenses for medical services provided by Intermountain Health.
The policy defines 'Fully Discounted Care' as a 100% waiver of patient financial obligation resulting from medical services provided by Intermountain Health.

The policy defines 'Discounted Care' as financial assistance that provides care at a discounted fee to eligible patients with annualized family incomes between amounts equal to or greater than 250% but less than or equal to 500% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines.

The policy defines 'Medical Hardship' as financial assistance that provides a discount based on a sliding scale to eligible patients with annualized family household income in excess of 500% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines and financial obligations resulting from medical services provided by any Intermountain Health entity or provider that exceed 25% of annualized family income.

The policy states that for Medical Hardship, the patient's Intermountain Health charges will be limited to 25% of their annual family income, and this charge adjustment will apply for all medical services qualified under this provision during a calendar year.

The policy lists eligibility criteria for presumptive eligibility including state-funded prescription programs, homelessness, participation in WIC, food stamp eligibility, subsidized school lunch program eligibility, eligibility for other state or local assistance programs, low income/subsidized housing, and eligibility based on health care industry sources of information.

The policy states that Intermountain Health may utilize a third-party predictive model based on public record databases to assess financial need and grant presumptive eligibility or relax documentation requirements.

The policy states that if a deceased patient is not married, has no established estate, and meets criteria for adjustment, the account will be routed for adjustment review; if the deceased has a surviving spouse, state law determines if the balance becomes the responsibility of the surviving spouse or the estate.
The policy excludes Mount Saint Vincent, Saltzer Health clinics, and Tellica Imaging locations from coverage.

The policy states that Intermountain Health will not charge patients eligible for financial assistance under this policy for emergency or other medically necessary care more than the AGB to individuals who have insurance.

The policy describes the look back method used to calculate AGB percentage at least annually by dividing the sum of all claims paid in full by Medicare and private health insurers by the sum of associated gross charges for those claims during the prior twelve-month period.
